map.destination: hero-synergy v0.1.0 fully decided: every question it depends on is resolved and every hard-to-reverse default has been challenged, so the result goes straight to `/to-spec`. The product is the VS Code Cockpit described in the seed. Its five capabilities are the outer bound: a ticket may cut one down, but nothing is added.
map.notes: Domain: an unofficial VS Code cockpit for Matt Pocock's agent skills. Plan, don't build: this map decides; the build comes afterwards. Seed tags: [E] items are requirements; [P] defaults stand as decided without a ticket. Skills: grilling tickets use `/grilling` and `/domain-modeling`; prototype tickets use `/prototype`; research tickets use `/research` and save findings in `docs/research/`. Writing to the repo: every ticket session works in its own git worktree and pushes its own edits to `main` after a rebase. ADRs: only for hard-to-reverse decisions. Toolchain: use `vp` for everything; run `vp check --fix` before pushing to `main`. Driver: Eduardo (`dbarjs`). A claim is an assignment to him.

decisions.title: Which wayfinder conventions exist in the wild?
decisions.gist: three generations upstream (single file, early tracker map, current map); old forms are recognizable by headings and `Status:` lines, legacy claim labels were never released, and the tracker templates still lag behind `SKILL.md`

decisions.title: Are the hero-synergy names free on npm, the Marketplace and Open VSX?
decisions.gist: the npm organization exists (almost certainly Eduardo's, unconfirmed); the unscoped npm name, both Marketplace publisher IDs and both Open VSX namespaces look free; the publisher ID can never be changed

decisions.title: Can one GraphQL query collect everything the scout needs?
decisions.gist: yes: one query returns a whole map for 6 rate-limit points, but `updatedAt` doesn't move when a parent or blocker is added, so relationships must be collected fresh every time

decisions.title: How do VS Code terminals and Claude Code hooks behave on Windows?
decisions.gist: by reading only: shell quoting, npm `.cmd` shims and a missing `SessionEnd` are the Windows risks; running `claude` as the terminal's own process avoids the quoting, and twelve items still need a real Windows test

decisions.title: How can a VS Code extension be integration-tested under Vite+?
decisions.gist: extension-host tests need Mocha through `@vscode/test-cli` as a separate script beside `vp test`; the webview is tested as a Vue app outside VS Code; real end-to-end means experimental Playwright on Electron

decisions.title: Which VS Code versions do Cursor, Windsurf and VSCodium ship?
decisions.gist: VSCodium is on 1.135, Cursor on 1.128, Windsurf on 1.126; the recommended floor is `^1.105.0`, set by the extension host's Node version rather than by any API

decisions.title: Scaffold the workspace
decisions.gist: on `main` and green in CI: Vite+ 1.0.0, Node 26.10, pnpm 12.8.1 and TypeScript 7 work together; the seed needed fourteen small corrections (missing `@vitejs/plugin-vue`, `@types/node`, `activationEvents` and a pnpm `allowBuilds` decision among them), and the devcontainer can't install the global `vp`

decisions.title: Which publisher ID and npm names?
decisions.gist: publisher `dbarjs` (created), so the extension ID is `dbarjs.hero-synergy` and the Open VSX namespace is `dbarjs`; the bare name `hero-synergy` belongs to the extension, the unscoped npm name is not claimed, and `@hero-synergy/core` and `@hero-synergy/cli` stand

decisions.title: Do the status hooks report a session's state reliably?
decisions.gist: yes, with a corrected table: the plugin stays and also hooks tool calls, `PermissionRequest` replaces the 6-second-late notification and tells a question from an approval, the terminal closing is the truth for "ended", and Esc is an accepted gap shown as time since the last status event

decisions.title: Does @effect/vitest 4 work with Vitest 5 under Vite+?
decisions.gist: yes, with no override and no peer warning: it shares the one Vitest 5.0.1 that Vite+ pins, on Node 24 and 26; Effect tests import from `@effect/vitest` instead of `vite-plus/test`

decisions.title: Which trackers and workspace shapes does v0.1.0 support?
decisions.gist: GitHub on github.com with native relationships, and local markdown; one repo per window, every open map shown; the tracker doc's heading decides which tracker is read; GitLab, "Other" trackers, closed maps and multi-root grouping are cut

decisions.title: What ships in v0.1.0 besides the extension?
decisions.gist: only the extension: the CLI is cut and its package removed, `@hero-synergy/core` stays a private workspace package bundled into the extension, nothing goes to npm, and Nitro has no role

decisions.title: zod or Effect Schema for the snapshot?
decisions.gist: Effect Schema for all boundary data, and zod is dropped: both libraries feed `claude -p --json-schema` and cost about 25 KB gzipped in the webview, so one library is enough; boundary data is plain JSON, the webview imports types only, and core exports no schema objects (ADR 0002)

decisions.title: How do a session's worktree edits get back to main?
decisions.gist: every ticket session gets `claude -w` and pushes its own edits straight to `main` after a rebase; the Cockpit never runs git or writes to the tracker, only shows each worktree's uncommitted and unpushed state (ADR 0003)

decisions.title: Which platforms and editors does v0.1.0 support?
decisions.gist: VS Code `^1.105.0` (`@types/vscode ~1.105.0`) on macOS and Linux, WSL remote as the Windows route, native Windows best-effort, forks not blocked but unsupported via Open VSX; README states Claude Code ≥ 2.1.139 and Node ≥ 22.18 on `PATH`; a session runs `claude` as the terminal's own process, never through a shell; no gating on editor or OS

notYetSpecified.text: The snapshot's fields. What a snapshot holds for each map and ticket, and which fields are facts from the tracker rather than a model's reading. It has to fit both trackers: a ticket is a URL on GitHub and a file path on a local tracker, and a local claim has no person. Waits on Which wayfinder conventions exist in the wild? and Does the scout's interpret step earn its place?
The scout budget. Refresh cadence, bundle size limits, cache keys, behavior on rate limits, and a fallback if `--safe-mode` changes. Waits on Does the scout's interpret step earn its place?

Scout against status hooks. When a session has claimed a ticket and the tracker doesn't show it yet, which side the Cockpit believes, and for how long. Status belongs to the ticket and its terminal, not to a session id, which changes on `/clear`. Waits on Does the scout's interpret step earn its place?
Actions in the Cockpit. Where actions sit, how the command is shown, and how the command name follows the install route (plugin or skills.sh). Waits on How do maps render in the Cockpit?

outOfScope.text: Building and releasing v0.1.0. The build, the release pipeline run and the one-time registry setup happen after this map.

A polished README for the extension and the repository. Comes after the v0.1.0 release; the release ships with the plain README the platform decision asks for. Tracked outside the map in Write a polished README for the extension and the repository

From the seed, for v0.1.0: a TUI; Claude Code's agent view; the official Claude Code VS Code extension; sandcastle and container sandboxes; agents other than Claude Code; writing to the tracker from the Cockpit; chaining user-invoked skills automatically; telemetry; a hosted service.

Trackers and workspace shapes, for v0.1.0: GitLab; "Other" trackers and the agentic collect step; any promise for GitHub Enterprise Server, the text fallbacks or cross-repo relationships; grouping maps per folder or a repo picker in a multi-root workspace; a folder holding several repos; closed maps. Ruled out in Which trackers and workspace shapes does v0.1.0 support?

Beyond the extension, for v0.1.0: the `@hero-synergy/cli` package and its commands; `@hero-synergy/core` as a public npm package; anything published to npm; Nitro, a browser Cockpit and a docs site. Ruled out in What ships in v0.1.0 besides the extension?

Platform verification, for v0.1.0: the twelve-item real-Windows test from the Windows research, and verifying terminals, icons and webview views inside Cursor, Devin Desktop and VSCodium. Ruled out in Which platforms and editors does v0.1.0 support?

ticket.question: A Cockpit session runs in its own worktree (`claude -w <ticket-slug>`). Grilling tickets edit `CONTEXT.md` and ADRs inline, so those edits land in the worktree. How do they get back to `main`, and who cleans up?
ticket.summary: How do a session's worktree edits get back to main?

resolution.author: dbarjs
resolution.gist: Every ticket session gets claude -w and pushes its own edits straight to main after a rebase; the Cockpit never runs git or writes to the tracker, only shows worktree state; local .scratch sessions run without -w; concurrent CONTEXT.md edits rebase and resolve conflict; removal is the user's hand or exit prompt; ADR 0003 records this

ticket.question: Does a small Claude Code plugin, loaded with `--plugin-dir`, give the Cockpit a trustworthy live status for a session?
ticket.summary: Do the status hooks report a session's state reliably?

resolution.author: dbarjs
resolution.gist: Yes, the plugin stays with a corrected table: started via SessionStart, working via UserPromptSubmit and tool use, waiting for you via Stop, needs approval via PermissionRequest, failed via StopFailure, ended via terminal closing; the plugin also hooks tool calls; Esc is an accepted gap; SessionEnd is a hint not the truth

ticket.question: Which of the names hero-synergy wants are free, taken, or already owned by Eduardo, and what are each registry's rules for claiming them?
ticket.summary: Are the hero-synergy names free on npm, the Marketplace and Open VSX?

resolution.author: dbarjs
resolution.gist: The npm organization exists (almost certainly Eduardo's); unscoped hero-synergy is free on npm; Marketplace publisher IDs hero-synergy and dbarjs are free; Open VSX namespaces are free; the publisher ID can never be changed after creation

ticket.question: Can a single `gh api graphql` query return everything the scout's collect step needs for every wayfinder issue in a repo?
ticket.summary: Can one GraphQL query collect everything the scout needs?

resolution.author: dbarjs
resolution.gist: Yes, one query returns all fields in 6 rate-limit points; updatedAt does not move when parent or blockers are added, so relationships must be collected fresh every time; pagination happens at 100 issues per page; REST is not needed as a fallback

ticket.question: Which conventions has `mattpocock/skills` shipped for wayfinder maps and tickets over time, and what does each one look like on a tracker?
ticket.summary: Which wayfinder conventions exist in the wild?

resolution.author: dbarjs
resolution.gist: Three generations: a single Markdown file (2026-06-15 to 2026-07-01), an early tracker map with Notes/Decisions/Fog (2026-07-01 to 2026-07-05, never released), and the current map with Destination/Notes/Decisions/Not yet specified/Out of scope (since 2026-07-05); claim moved from wayfinder:claimed label to assignee; fallbacks are Part of #map in task list and Blocked by: lines; local format uses Status: claimed|resolved

ticket.question: What breaks, or needs different handling, when the Cockpit launches sessions and reads status events on Windows?
ticket.summary: How do VS Code terminals and Claude Code hooks behave on Windows?

resolution.author: dbarjs
resolution.gist: Running claude as the terminal's process avoids shell quoting issues; npm .cmd shims cannot be spawned by child_process without a shell; SessionEnd may never fire on Windows; exec-form hooks with node and CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT need Claude Code 2.1.139 or later; twelve concrete items still need real Windows testing

ticket.question: Which VS Code API version does each fork currently ship, and what is the lowest `engines.vscode` that still gives the Cockpit the APIs it needs?
ticket.summary: Which VS Code versions do Cursor, Windsurf and VSCodium ship?

resolution.author: dbarjs
resolution.gist: VSCodium 1.135, Cursor 1.128, Windsurf 1.126; every API landed by 1.93 but Node sets the floor: 1.105 is the first version all forks ship on Node >= 22.18, so engines.vscode ^1.105.0 with @types/vscode ~1.105.0

ticket.question: What are the working ways to integration-test a VS Code extension today, and do they fit a Vite+ workspace?

resolution.author: dbarjs
resolution.gist: Extension-host tests need Mocha through @vscode/test-cli as a separate script; webview is tested as a Vue app outside VS Code; real end-to-end means experimental Playwright on Electron; no first-party Vitest route into the extension host exists

ticket.question: Does `@effect/vitest` 4.0.0 run under the Vitest 5 that Vite+ bundles?

resolution.author: dbarjs
resolution.gist: Yes, with no override and no peer-dependency warning; @effect/vitest 4.0.0 runs under Vitest 5.0.1 that Vite+ pins; Effect tests import from @effect/vitest instead of vite-plus/test; both resolve to the same Vitest instance

ticket.question: Which library models the data that crosses a boundary (the snapshot, config, webview messages): zod, Effect Schema, or both?
